resourceName: DIT AgTech grouped project: reduction of enteric methane emissions from livestock production systems via the uDOSE water medication technology.
description:
The DIT AgTech grouped project for ‘the reduction of enteric methane emissions from livestock production systems via the uDOSE water medication technology’, will supply a methane reducing feed ingredient (ie Agolin Ruminant L®) through the drinking water of ruminant livestock production systems. This will be achieved by using the uDOSE/uHUB technology already developed by DIT AgTech for the feeding of methane reducing feed additives and the subsequent monitoring, recording and accounting for resultant reduction of GHG emissions.

The uDOSE technology system is designed to accurately and automatically administer a predetermined dosage of supplement into the drinking water of livestock. This ensures that each animal receives a targeted dose proportionate to its body weight. Unlike the consumption of dry feed, where herd-level behavioral competition can lead to inconsistent intake of feed additives and waste due to exposure to environmental conditions, every animal drinks water in proportion to its body weight daily. The uDOSE is connected via satellite enabling bidirectional communication with the uHUB system that constantly monitors, records and controls the dosing activities in real time.

Backed up by the research from CQUniversity (Batley, R. (2023)), the uDOSE system has been proven to be an effective way to mitigate methane production in a livestock production system and therefore proposes a variation to the VM0041 methodology which currently only describes the feeding of methane reducing feed additives to livestock through dry feed.
